stages.title: JANA TO JANAPADA: TERRITORIAL POLITICAL CHANGE

pills.text: STRONGER KINGSHIP LINEAGE LOYALTY FIELDS/CLAIMS BOUNDED PEOPLES SHARE, FORCE

stages.answer_line: The movement from jana (people/tribal community) to janapada (territorial foothold/domain of a people) rescaled kinship into territorial politics without erasing lineage, assemblies or regional alternatives.

stages.answer_line: Later Vedic religion combined domestic practice with increasingly specialised śrauta (solemn public sacrifice) ritual, changing deity emphasis and a priestly political economy; Indra and Agni changed in relative prominence rather than disappearing.

pills.text: POWER/PRESTIGE REDISTRIBUTES GIFTS/ANIMALS RANKS RULER, PRIESTS AND PARTICIPANTS

ASHVAMEDHA: sovereignty
VAJAPEYA: power/prestige redistributes gifts/animals ranks ruler, priests and participants
Ritual stages, legitimises and negotiates power; it does not merely reflect it.

stages.answer_line: Rājasūya (royal consecration), aśvamedha (horse sacrifice and paramountcy claim) and vājapeya (ritual of strength and prestige) mobilised and redistributed surplus while staging sovereignty that could exceed actual territorial control.

stages.title: UPANISHADIC TURN: RITUAL TRANSFORMED INWARD

pills.text: SACRIFICE PROMISES RESULTS BUT LEAVES DEATH, SELF AND ULTIMATE
KARMA/REBIRTH + BRAHMAN-ATMAN INQUIRY + KNOWLEDGE AS LIBERATING DISCIPLINE
UPANISHADIC THOUGHT GROWS WITHIN AND TRANSFORMS VEDIC TRADITION.

sequence: PROBLEM: sacrifice promises results but leaves death, self and ultimate reality open.
karma/rebirth + brahman-atman inquiry + knowledge as liberating discipline internalisation of sacrifice critique/reinterpretation of ritual
Not total rejection: Upanishadic thought grows within and transforms Vedic tradition.
